businessRules.rule: An exam covers named classes and subjects. A subject not attached to the class cannot be examined in it.

Every subject in the exam carries its own total marks, passing marks and maximum grace marks. A single figure across an exam does not survive contact with a practical paper worth 30 and a theory paper worth 70.

Those three figures are fixed when the exam is created and cannot be changed afterwards. Marks entry and grade calculation both read them, and a rule that moves after marks are entered makes every earlier entry unexplainable.
A paper is either assembled from the question bank or authored by the subject teacher and submitted to the Coordinator, who reviews it. A paper nobody reviewed reaches the hall unchecked.
Each scheduled paper carries a marks-upload deadline for its teacher, on or after the paper date. A deadline is what makes the completeness check in marks entry mean anything.
The Coordinator creates and schedules; the School Admin approves. The schedule cannot be published until that approval is given.
On approval the schedule is published to the Principal, the teachers, the students and their guardians in one act.

Each teacher's notification lists their own duties for the exam — the papers they invigilate, the papers they mark, and their upload deadline. A teacher told only the dates has to work out their own part from a timetable.
The School Admin may edit an already published schedule. Every affected teacher, student and guardian is notified of the change, and the change carries a reason.
A paper is not scheduled on a day the school is closed, nor may two papers for the same class overlap in time.
Creating an exam produces no marks and no results. It schedules an exam; it examines nobody.
An exam is never deleted. An exam that will not run is cancelled, and its schedule and approvals stay readable.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Examination → Exams → Create New Exam
basicFlow.userAction: Gives the exam a name, a code, its session and start date, and selects the classes and subjects it covers.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the code is unique in the session and that every subject belongs to its class.

basicFlow.userAction: Sets the total marks, the passing marks and the maximum grace marks for each subject.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Validates that passing marks are below the total, and fixes the three figures for the life of the exam.

basicFlow.userAction: Assembles a paper from the question bank, or the subject teacher authors one and submits it for review.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Attaches the paper to the subject, holding a teacher-authored paper for the Coordinator's review.

basicFlow.userAction: Schedules each paper to a date, a time slot and a duration, and sets that subject's marks-upload deadline.
basicFlow.function: schedulePaper(examId, subjectId, date, slot, duration, marksDeadline, invigilatorId)
basicFlow.systemResponse: Refuses a closed day or a clash with another paper for the same class, and checks the deadline is on or after the paper date.

basicFlow.userAction: Submits the exam and its schedule.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Holds it at Awaiting approval. Nothing is published in the meantime.

basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the exam and its schedule and approves it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval, which is what permits publication.
Publishes to the Principal, the teachers, the students and their guardians, and tells each teacher their own duties and deadline.

basicFlow.userAction: Changes a published schedule where a date or a slot has to move.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Applies the change with its reason and notifies every affected teacher, student and guardian.

alternateFlows.condition: The subject teacher authors the paper
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Examination → My exam duties → Submit paper
alternateFlows.behaviour: The teacher writes the paper for their own subject and submits it. The Coordinator reviews it before it is attached, so no paper reaches the hall unchecked (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: The paper is assembled from the question bank
alternateFlows.navigation: Paper schedule → Assign paper → Question bank
alternateFlows.behaviour: The paper is built from the bank rather than authored, and is attached directly.

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin does not approve
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns to the Coordinator and nothing is published. Students and families learn nothing of a schedule that was not agreed.

alternateFlows.condition: A paper has to move after publication
alternateFlows.behaviour: The change carries a reason and every affected teacher, student and guardian is notified. A changed date nobody was told about is worse than no schedule (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The chosen date is a holiday or clashes with another paper
alternateFlows.behaviour: The slot is refused and another is chosen. A class cannot sit two papers at once (BR-10).
alternateFlows.function: schedulePaper(examId, subjectId, date, slot, duration, marksDeadline, invigilatorId)

alternateFlows.condition: The exam will not run after all
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is cancelled rather than deleted, everybody concerned is notified, and its schedule and approvals stay readable (BR-12).

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
